best_for: YouTubers, teachers and hobby editors who want a free video editor with multicam, proxies and color scopes, and whose computer has a decent CPU.
description:
Kdenlive, short for KDE Non-Linear Video Editor, is a video editor that Jason Wood started in 2003. Jean-Baptiste Mardelle has led it since 2006, and it became an official KDE app in 2015. A small team, mostly volunteers, keeps it going, with no registration and no paid extras to unlock.

You can bring in footage in almost any audio or video format, tag it, filter it and sort it into several bins. Mark key moments on the timeline, and let automatic backups guard your project. Record a voiceover inside the app, balance sound with the mixers and watch the audio spectrum. Check color with a histogram and RGB parade, add title clips, and send complex motion graphics to Glaxnimate.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Kdenlive is free under the GPL and runs on Linux, Windows, macOS and BSD.

points.title: More than cuts
points.text: The timeline supports multicam, nested sequences and 3-point editing. Hundreds of effects take keyframes, and color tools include LUTs, grading and scopes such as a vectorscope and waveform.

points.title: Subtitles from speech
points.text: Automatic transcription turns spoken audio into subtitles, which saves typing captions by hand.

points.title: Your CPU does the playback
points.text: Timeline playback runs on the CPU. The manual suggests 4 cores and 8 GB of RAM for HD, and 8 cores and 16 GB for 4K. On a slow machine, proxy clips and preview rendering keep playback smooth.

points.title: Requirements by system
points.text: The manual lists 64-bit Windows 10 version 1809 or later, 64-bit Linux, and macOS 13 or later on Apple Silicon. The download page also offers an Intel Mac build, also for macOS 13 or later.

points.title: Where older versions are
points.text: The Windows installer can install per-user or for all users, and the Windows listing keeps 50 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release. Kdenlive keeps an archive of older builds for projects that break on an update.

points.title: Linux Flatpak from KDE
points.text: The Flathub build is published by KDE and marked verified, for x64 and Arm64. The project also offers an AppImage.
